newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco, Calif., PUC bonds Aa - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco, Calif., PUC bonds Aa - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service announced today that it has reviewed and confirmed the Aa rating on the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Water Revenue Bonds.

The PUC, which provides water to 755,300 city residents and wholesale water to agencies serving 1.5 million suburban residents in San Mateo, Santa Clara and Alameda Counties, is expected to sell $131.3 million of Water Revenue Bonds through a competitive sale scheduled for December 3rd.
According to Moody's, "The high quality rating is based on the strength of the large, diverse service area, secure source of high quality water, relatively low rates and strong coverage levels."

In confirming the rating, however, Moody's cautioned that the commission is in the process of developing a water supply master plan and a ten-year Capital Improvement Program which could result in the need for significant additional borrowing and significant rate increases over an extended period of time.

Moody's indicated that it would continue to assess the CIP, which will principally address seismic and reliability issues, as it is developed and indicated that the mix of financing for the program and pace of the program could have important implications for future rates and debt service coverage.

Moody's also cautioned that City Charter changes enacted this summer, altering the rate-setting process, and the adoption of the state-wide Proposition 218 have altered the PUC's rate-setting environment as these increases are being contemplated.

While noting that Proposition 218 may now create mechanisms by which citizens may block rate increases or reduce existing rates, Moody's noted specific political considerations provide comfort regarding these risks in San Francisco.

Among these factors noted by Moody's are the PUC's plans to seek voter approval next year for the next phase of its capital program, the history of voter support in the city for seismic upgrade programs, the mix of retail and wholesale payers, the apparent absence of substantive change in the existing initiative process from prior Charter provisions, and San Francisco voters' opposition to Proposition 218 earlier this month.

The 1996 bonds are issued on parity with $145,550,000 of outstanding Series 1987, 1991 and 1992 bonds. Proceeds will be used to refund Series 1991 bonds maturing 2004 through 2020 and provide new money for capital projects.
